title: Geometry - Lesson 1 Practice: Choosing Units
description: Practice selecting suitable units for volume and capacity.

questions.question: Which unit is most suitable for the volume of a small cube?
questions.explanation: A small cube is a 3D solid, so cubic centimeters are suitable.

questions.question: Which unit is most suitable for the capacity of a water bottle?
questions.explanation: A water bottle holds liquid, so liters are a suitable capacity unit.

questions.question: cm² is a suitable unit for volume.
questions.explanation: cm² measures area. Volume uses cubic units such as cm³.

questions.question: The capacity of a medicine cup is usually measured in ______.
questions.explanation: A medicine cup holds a small amount of liquid, so milliliters are suitable.

questions.question: Which unit is most suitable for the volume of a classroom?
questions.explanation: A classroom is a large 3D space, so cubic meters are suitable.

questions.question: Explain why liters are better than square centimeters for the capacity of a pitcher.
questions.correctAnswer: Liters are better because capacity measures how much liquid a container holds, while square centimeters measure flat area.
questions.explanation: The pitcher holds liquid, so it needs a capacity unit. cm² measures surface area, not liquid amount.

questions.question: Which object would most likely be measured in milliliters?
questions.explanation: A spoonful of syrup is a small liquid amount, so milliliters fit best.

questions.question: Choose a suitable unit for the volume of a shoebox and explain your choice.
questions.correctAnswer: cm³, because a shoebox is a small 3D space and volume uses cubic units.
questions.explanation: A shoebox is a solid 3D object, so a cubic unit such as cm³ is suitable.
